title: Square Root Calculator: how it works, formula and examples
excerpt: Square Root Calculator: Square root, cube root and nth root. Learn how to use it, the formula behind it, a worked example and answers to common questions.
content:
The [Square Root Calculator](/square-root-calculator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Square root, cube root and nth root. Enter your number and root (n) and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

The square root of a number is the value that, multiplied by itself, gives the original number. This calculator also finds cube roots and any nth root. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers. Related Math tools include [Percentage Calculator](/percentage-calculator), [Fraction Calculator](/fraction-calculator) and [Average Calculator](/average-calculator).

## How to use the Square Root Calculator

Start by entering your number, then entering your root (n). The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. When you want a clean slate, Reset restores the defaults.

1. Enter your number.
2. Enter your root (n).
3. Check the result — it updates instantly as you type.
4. Use Reset to start over with the default values.

## Formula

√x = x^(1/2). ∛x = x^(1/3). ⁿ√x = x^(1/n).

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Square Root Calculator](/square-root-calculator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic. If the figures look wrong, check your inputs first — a misplaced decimal point is the usual culprit.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. √144 = 12, ∛27 = 3, and the 4th root of 81 is 3. Try the same figures in the [Square Root Calculator](/square-root-calculator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves. The steps are the same whatever numbers you use; only the figures change.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Number: 144, Root (n): 2), the [Square Root Calculator](/square-root-calculator) returns 2th root: 12, Square root: 12, Cube root: 5.24148279, Square: 20,736. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. Change any value and every figure updates instantly. If you want to compare with a related calculation, the [Percentage Calculator](/percentage-calculator) is worth a look before you finish.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Perfect squares: 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36, 49, 64, 81, 100…
- Negative numbers have no real square root.

Keep these in mind and the figures will be as useful as the numbers you put in.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is the square root of 2?

Approximately 1.41421356 — it's irrational. Try it with your own numbers in the [Square Root Calculator](/square-root-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Can a number have two square roots?

Yes, ±. The calculator shows the principal (positive) root. Try it with your own numbers in the [Square Root Calculator](/square-root-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What formula does the Square Root Calculator use?

√x = x^(1/2). ∛x = x^(1/3). ⁿ√x = x^(1/n). You can see it in action in the [Square Root Calculator](/square-root-calculator) — enter your own values and the result updates as you type.

### What do I need to use the Square Root Calculator?

Just Number and Root (n). Enter those values and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.
